The following solution to the single producer single consumer problem uses semaphores for synchronization.

#define BUFFSIZE 100
buffer buf[BUFFSIZE];
int first = last = 0;
semaphore b_full = 0;
semaphore b_empty = BUFFSIZE
void producer()
{
    while(1)
    {
        produce an item;
        P1:.................;
        put the item into buff (first);
        first = (first+1)%BUFFSIZE;
        P2: ...............;
    }
}
void consumer()
{
    while(1)
    {
        C1:............;
        take the item from buf[last];
        last = (last+1)%BUFFSIZE;
        C2:............;
        consume the item;
    }
}

The right choice of values for above four empty lines labeled as P1, P2, C1 and C2 is:

  1. P1: P(Empty) P2: V(Full) C1: P(Empty) C2: V(Full)
  2. P1: P(Full) P2: V(Empty) C1: P(Full) C2: V(Empty)
  3. P1: P(Empty) P2: V(Full) C1: P(Full) C2: V(Empty)
  4. P1: P(Full) P2: V(Empty) C1: P(Empty) C2: V(Full)

Consider following Cigarette smokers problem:
Assume a cigarette requires three ingredients to make and smoke: tobacco, paper, and matches. There are three smokers A,B and C around a table, each of whom has an infinite supply of one of the three ingredients — one smoker B has an infinite supply of tobacco, C  has paper, and A has matches. All smokers are sleeping initially.
There is a non-smoking agent who enables the smokers to make their cigarettes by arbitrarily selecting two of the supplies to place on the table, wakes up the smoker who has the third ingredient and then sleeps immediately. The smoker who has the third supply removes the two items from the table, using them (along with his own supply) he makes a cigarette then he smokes for a while. Once the cigarette is finished, the smoker wakes up the agent and goes to sleep indefinitely. The agent places two new random items on the table. This process continues forever.
The minimum number of semaphores required to handle this problem is _________

Narendra is trapped on a dry island and he needs to chemically generate water using Hydrogen and Oxygen taken from the environment. He needs to get two H atoms and one O atom all together at the same time. Each atom is a thread. Each H atom invokes a procedure $\textit{hReady}$ when it is ready to react and each O atom invokes a procedure $\textit{oReady}$ when it is ready. The procedures must delay until there are at least two H atoms and one O atom present and then one of the threads must call the procedure $\textit{makeWater}$ (which just prints out a debug message that water was made). After the $\textit{makeWater}$ call, two instances of $\textit{hReady}$ and one instance of $\textit{oReady}$ should return.
An algorithm is peoposed to solve this problem as shown below. The semaphore implementation enforces FIFO order for wake up, i.e. the thread waiting longest in P() is always the next thread woken up by a call to V().

Semaphore h_wait = 0;
Semaphore o_wait = 0;
int count = 0;
hReady()
{
    count++;
    if(count %2 == 1)
    {
        P(h_wait);
    }
    else
    {
        V(o_wait);
        P(h_wait);
    }
return;
}
oReady()
{
    P(o_wait);
    makeWater();
    V(h_wait);
    V(h_wait);
return;
}

What could be said about this proposed solution?

  1. The solution solves the problem fine.
  2. The solution leads to deadlock.
  3. The solution may not always solve the problem.
  4. None of the above
